scenes.tts: The first film tracked one domain to its target. What changes when one protein carries several binding modules? Those modules can now influence one another's effects.
scenes.caption: The first film tracked one domain to its target. What changes when one protein carries several binding modules? Those modules can now influence one another's effects.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's COLOR MAP exactly: proteins blue, phosphates gold, binding domains teal, matching motifs green, failed contacts red. A single teal reader on a blue host duplicates into two differently shaped teal modules on one long blue protein. Mark every molecular cartoon schematic.
scenes.narration: The first film tracked one domain to its target. What changes when one protein carries several binding modules? Those modules can now influence one another's effects.

scenes.visual: Keep the long blue protein moving gently behind a brief title: Two Grips, One Decision. Fade the title and preserve the protein's position.

scenes.tts: Start with cellular Sark as an open strip. It carries an S H three domain, an S H two domain, a kinase, and a short tail. Each block keeps a distinct job. Flexible connections let those blocks meet within one protein.
scenes.caption: Start with cellular Src as an open strip. It carries an SH3 domain, an SH2 domain, a kinase, and a short tail. Each block keeps a distinct job. Flexible connections let those blocks meet within one protein.
scenes.visual: Build one large horizontal schematic Src strip from left to right. Add teal blocks labelled SH3 and SH2, a blue kinase block, and a flexible blue tail. Keep labels large and the protein filling most of the frame.
scenes.narration: Start with cellular Src as an open strip. It carries an SH3 domain, an SH2 domain, a kinase, and a short tail. Each block keeps a distinct job. Flexible connections let those blocks meet within one protein.

scenes.tts: A kinase called C S K places phosphate on a tail tyrosine. The tail bends back. Sark's own S H two pocket catches that phosphotyrosine, bringing the tail against the protein. This contact uses the reader internally.
scenes.caption: A kinase called Csk places phosphate on a tail tyrosine. The tail bends back. Src's own SH2 pocket catches that phosphotyrosine, bringing the tail against the protein. This contact uses the reader internally.
scenes.visual: A small Csk label approaches, then a gold badge appears on the tail. Remove Csk. Curve the tail back across the kinase until its gold badge settles into the teal SH2 pocket.
scenes.narration: A kinase called Csk places phosphate on a tail tyrosine. The tail bends back. Src's own SH2 pocket catches that phosphotyrosine, bringing the tail against the protein. This contact uses the reader internally.

scenes.tts: The S H three domain catches the linker at the same time. These internal contacts settle both domains against the kinase. Together they stabilize an inactive shape. Neither module performs the kinase reaction itself.
scenes.caption: The SH3 domain catches the linker at the same time. These internal contacts settle both domains against the kinase. Together they stabilize an inactive shape. Neither module performs the kinase reaction itself.
scenes.visual: Highlight the linker segment in green and fold it into the teal SH3 groove. Transform the open strip into a compact clamp around the blue kinase. Dim the kinase without crossing it out; label inactive shape, schematic.
scenes.narration: The SH3 domain catches the linker at the same time. These internal contacts settle both domains against the kinase. Together they stabilize an inactive shape. Neither module performs the kinase reaction itself.

scenes.tts: Now offer the S H two domain a better external phosphotyrosine target. Predict what happens. Can Sark's own tail still complete the same grip? Compare the two targets competing for one pocket.
scenes.caption: Now offer the SH2 domain a better external phosphotyrosine target. Predict what happens. Can Src's own tail still complete the same grip? Compare the two targets competing for one pocket.
scenes.visual: Bring in a large external blue target with a gold badge and fitting green neighbors. Hold it beside the occupied SH2 domain. Display Can the tail keep the same grip? Keep the compact Src clamp otherwise unchanged.
scenes.narration: Now offer the SH2 domain a better external phosphotyrosine target. Predict what happens. Can Src's own tail still complete the same grip? Compare the two targets competing for one pocket.

scenes.visual: Hold the prediction layout. Let the external target drift slightly closer while Src's tail and SH2 pocket remain connected. Do not reveal displacement during the pause.

scenes.tts: No. The external target can occupy S H two and pull it from the tail. Losing one internal contact loosens the clamp. Other inputs can also disturb the S H three contact. Opening makes kinase activation more accessible.
scenes.caption: No. The external target can occupy SH2 and pull it from the tail. Losing one internal contact loosens the clamp. Other inputs can also disturb the SH3 contact. Opening makes kinase activation more accessible.
scenes.visual: Move the external gold-and-green target into SH2 as the tail slides free. Partly unfold Src and brighten the kinase, labelled clamp loosened. Briefly show an unlabeled external green motif tugging at SH3, without declaring full activation.
scenes.narration: No. The external target can occupy SH2 and pull it from the tail. Losing one internal contact loosens the clamp. Other inputs can also disturb the SH3 contact. Opening makes kinase activation more accessible.

scenes.tts: Viral Sark has lost the tail and its regulatory tyrosine, along with other mutations. Without that tail contact, the full internal clamp cannot form, so the kinase is always on. The missing module target removes an off-switch.
scenes.caption: Viral Src has lost the tail and its regulatory tyrosine, along with other mutations. Without that tail contact, the full internal clamp cannot form, so the kinase is always on. The missing module target removes an off-switch.
scenes.visual: Place cellular Src and viral Src side by side. On viral Src, transform the long strip into a shorter one lacking the tail; show small neutral ticks for other mutations. The tail-less kinase stays bright.
scenes.narration: Viral Src has lost the tail and its regulatory tyrosine, along with other mutations. Without that tail contact, the full internal clamp cannot form, so the kinase is always on. The missing module target removes an off-switch.

scenes.tts: The same modular logic can build a conditional detector. Give one protein an S H two domain for a phosphorylated receptor. Add a P H domain for a membrane lipid. Join them with a flexible linker.
scenes.caption: The same modular logic can build a conditional detector. Give one protein an SH2 domain for a phosphorylated receptor and a PH domain for a membrane lipid. Join them with a flexible linker.
scenes.visual: Transform Src's two teal modules into an abstract blue detector carrying teal SH2 and PH blocks. Bring back the blue receptor with a gold site above a membrane bar. Add one green lipid target in the membrane. Mark the layout schematic.
scenes.narration: The same modular logic can build a conditional detector. Give one protein an SH2 domain for a phosphorylated receptor and a PH domain for a membrane lipid. Join them with a flexible linker.

scenes.tts: Suppose either contact alone is too weak to retain the detector. With only the receptor mark, it visits and leaves. With only the lipid, it also visits and leaves. One input produces only a brief encounter.
scenes.caption: Suppose either contact alone is too weak to retain the detector. With only the receptor mark, it visits and leaves. With only the lipid, it also visits and leaves. One input produces only a brief encounter.
scenes.visual: Run two side-by-side cases. In the first, SH2 touches the gold receptor site and releases. Reset fully. In the second, PH touches the green lipid and releases. Use weak grip labels, never failed or rejected.
scenes.narration: Suppose either contact alone is too weak to retain the detector. With only the receptor mark, it visits and leaves. With only the lipid, it also visits and leaves. One input produces only a brief encounter.

scenes.tts: When both targets are close, both domains bind at once. Each contact helps keep the other within reach. The detector remains recruited only where the two inputs coincide. Removing either target again releases it. This joint retention is avidity: two weak contacts together can behave like one much tighter interaction at that location.
scenes.caption: When both targets are close, both domains bind at once. Each contact helps keep the other within reach. The detector remains recruited only where the two inputs coincide. Removing either target again releases it. This joint retention is avidity: two weak contacts together can behave like one much tighter interaction at that location.
scenes.visual: Reset to one membrane region containing both targets. Bind SH2 to the gold receptor site and PH to the green lipid together. Thicken both connection lines and keep the detector localized while nearby single-target regions remain transient. Add a teal brace labelled avidity around the two contacts.
scenes.narration: When both targets are close, both domains bind at once. Each contact helps keep the other within reach. The detector remains recruited only where the two inputs coincide. Removing either target again releases it. This joint retention is avidity: two weak contacts together can behave like one much tighter interaction at that location.

scenes.tts: That is the second rule. Combining modules can make binding conditional on more than one signal. In Sark, two internal contacts together hold the kinase off. In the detector, two external contacts together hold the protein in place.
scenes.caption: That is the second rule. Combining modules can make binding conditional on more than one signal. In Src, two internal contacts together hold the kinase off. In the detector, two external contacts together hold the protein in place.
scenes.visual: Split the frame between compact Src on the left and the two-input detector on the right. Draw a teal brace around Src's two internal contacts, labelled holds off, and around the detector's two external contacts, labelled holds in place. Place the rule across the top and keep both cartoons moving gently.
scenes.narration: That is the second rule. Combining modules can make binding conditional on more than one signal. In Src, two internal contacts together hold the kinase off. In the detector, two external contacts together hold the protein in place.

scenes.visual: One-line end card only, centered in large type: 'Combining modules can make binding conditional on more than one signal.' No subtitle, logo, teaser, or second line.
